originalLevelChart.speedBasis: Original horizontal axis explicitly TRUE AIRSPEED - KNOTS

originalClimbChart.note: Gross weight 12,500 lb. Normal and military rate and time-to-climb curves confirmed. No numeric time curve extracted.

corsair.engineQualification: Rating altitudes are a secondary transcription of the March 1946 Navy chart, with manufacturer normal-power/rpm and 20:9 gearing corroboration. Original AAHS PDF located but rating cells not independently digitized. Generic inlet recovery 0.85 and fixed gear-transition heights are assumptions. Power-on stall throttle setting and exact stall pressure altitude unknown.
corsair.fit: Normal sea-level speed for drag and normal sea-level maximum climb for equivalent low-J installation loss. Clean off/on stall CAS values are lift anchors.
corsair.check: All military points and normal altitude points excluded from numerical fitting. Same report, exposed before tuning, not independent.
corsair.calibrationMeaning: Equivalent propulsive loss adjustment with full-shaft ideal-disk bound. Does not isolate blade efficiency, engine-chart error, cooling or airframe interaction.
corsair.geometryQualification: Manufacturer F4U-4 page gives 40.90 ft span; 314 sqft from USN naval aircraft appendix. Generic profile geometry, not a measured span of 80765.

p47.fit: December 41-5942 5,000-ft speed difference and 10,000-ft climb difference. No January cuff/CG/speed-basis transfer.
p47.check: December climb differences at 15,000, 20,000 and 24,000 ft and speed at 25,000 ft; same-report held-out conditions.

mustang.fit: Same 43-24777 clean and racked 75-inHg 20,800-ft speed pair.
mustang.check: 67-inHg racked 20,800-ft speed, same report and previously exposed.
mustang.qualification: Packard chart BHP. Mass changes due to rack removal unknown, equivalent drag-area fit holds model mass constant.

fuel.status: Engineering scenario, not a measured fuel curve
fuel.method: Midpoint integration, 10 altitude segments with midpoint weight iteration; generic best-climb speed reoptimized at each segment.
